title: Blood Test Shows Concussion Injury

image.attribution: University of the Fraser Valley / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-2.0

main_content:
A new blood test can tell doctors whether a person has suffered a concussion up to a week after he or she was injured.

A study describing the test was published in the journal JAMA Neurology.

People who suffer a head injury should rest soon after they are hurt.

Individuals who have suffered a concussion do not always show symptoms. Experts say those signs can be delayed, especially in children.

A concussion can lead to a feeling of dizziness, headaches, and an inability to sleep. These problems can exist for a long time.

Doctors at Orlando Health System in Florida developed the new blood test. It shows if a biomarker is in a person’s blood.

Researchers examined the blood of 600 patients. They found the biomarker in the blood of those who had suffered a head injury.

Concussion is a common injury in sports. A blood test soon after a head injury could show if an athlete has suffered a concussion.

questions.question: Do people who had a concussion always show symptoms?
options: A) Yes, symptoms are always present immediately after injury.
B) No, symptoms can be delayed and may not appear at all.
C) Yes, they show symptoms only in adults.
D) No, only children experience delayed symptoms.
questions.answer: B) No, symptoms can be delayed and may not appear at all.

questions.question: What can a concussion lead to?
options: A) A feeling of dizziness and headaches.
B) Immediate and permanent vision loss.
C) Improved cognitive function after recovery.
questions.answer: A) A feeling of dizziness and headaches.

questions.question: What is found in the blood of people who had a concussion?
options: A) A deficiency of red blood cells.
C) A specific biomarker indicating a head injury.
D) Antibodies developed from previous injuries.
questions.answer: C) A specific biomarker indicating a head injury.
